computation_method: Host python3 exact integer arithmetic plus 60-digit Decimal logarithms. No candidate package Python was executed on the host. All identities in certificate.json re-run from the protected target-profile.json constants. Factorization found cold by trial division to 2^26 plus Pollard rho; primality by trial division and deterministic Miller-Rabin; xi=7 primitive-root test over the full factorization of r-1.
key_finding: q = (r-1)/2^20 is fully smooth: q = 2^12 * 3 * 11 * 19 * 10177 * 125527 * 859267 * 906349^2 * 2508409 * 2529403 * 52437899 * 254760293^2, product reconstructs q exactly (cert P1), largest prime 254760293 < 2^28 (cert P2). The staged v3 package's 2*m1 ~ 2^118.43 generic phase-1 grid is therefore replaceable by Pohlig-Hellman digit grids of at most 2*ceil(sqrt(254760293)) = 31924 additions each.

ledger.scalar_mult_itemization: B1=[zeta]P0 (1); Y=[q/l^e]A_d per prime (12); B_l=[q/l^e]B1 per prime (12); per-digit [l]-map plus fold-add scalar point (2*25=50); T'=[xi^-k2]T, B2=[delta]P0, verify [s]P0=T (3); total 78 at the 512-addition 255-bit double-and-add upper bound

memory_reported_not_charged.model: largest digit table: 2*15962 slots (load factor 1/2) x 56-byte packed records = 1787744 bytes, plus 2^16 challenge/code margin; digit tables sequential, peak = max single table

success_probability.basis: Every digit grid satisfies m_l^2 >= l (cert P8) and the phase-2 grid m2^2 = d (cert P10); the s = xi^(q*k1+k2) decomposition bijects (cert P9); CRT over coprime prime powers of q is exact; final verification [s]P0=T gates output. Exhaustive grids, no random walks, no Poisson heuristic.

staged_comparison.finding_vs_staged: Staged v3 treats q as generic and pays 2*ceil(sqrt(q)) ~ 2^118.43 for phase 1; q is in fact fully 28-bit-smooth (cert P1-P4), so digit-by-digit Pohlig-Hellman replaces the grid at 91330 additions. Same C=2000, same 500-instruction hash budget, same 512-addition scalar-mul bound as staged v3; nothing inherited.
